title: tool-composition-api: ergonomic surface for parallel tool runs, injection semantics, and retry policies
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Introduces a new ergonomic API for multi-tool invocation: tool_batch and tool_inject semantics with configurable retry and idempotency controls. Backwards-compatible with existing OpenAI-compat layer. See migration notes in docs/cli and SDK updates.
description: Motivation: customers build richer chains that call multiple tools concurrently (search, DB read, action runner) and need predictable ordering, deterministic injection of tool outputs into model prompts, and controlled retry semantics for transient tool failures. Current surfaces force users to implement orchestration in application code resulting in duplicated logic and inconsistent behaviors across SDKs. This PR adds a compact, language-agnostic surface to ergonomically express parallel tool runs, result injection semantics, and retry policies while preserving streaming stability and OpenAI-compat behavior. Summary of changes: 1) New top-level request fields `tool_batch` (list) and `tool_run_mode` (parallel | sequential | ordered-parallel) that let callers declare multiple tool calls in a single generation request. 2) `inject_results` (none | inline | metadata) controls how tool outputs appear in the returned token stream: inline injects textual content into the model response stream at the injection point; metadata returns a structured envelope alongside tokens for programmatic consumers. 3) `retry_policy` per-tool with backoff and idempotency_token: default is up to 2 retries on transient 5xx/429 with exponential jitter. 4) Deterministic ordering guarantees for ordered-parallel mode: results are delivered in the declared order regardless of completion time, with streaming placeholders and progress events emitted to preserve low latency streaming. 5) OpenAI-compat layer: the legacy `function_call` field maps into `tool_batch` with `inject_results=inline` by default, preserving backward compatibility; we add a compatibility toggle `compat.openai_tool_integration: true|false`. 6) SDK updates: Python/TS SDKs expose a new `tools` param and helper `ToolSpec` to build idempotent calls; examples and templates included. 7) Observability: new metrics for tool latency, tool_retry_count, tool_concurrency, and streaming_injection_errors. 8) Error semantics: if all retries fail for a required tool the request fails with a structured error; optional tools return null payloads and include partial_reason in metadata. Checklist: - [x] API design doc linked in ENG-3221 - [x] Server-side implementation of orchestration and scheduler - [x] Streaming integration tests for ordered-parallel and parallel paths - [x] SDK bindings for Python and TypeScript - [x] Docs and migration guide - [x] QA smoke test run against Dedicated cluster - [x] Performance microbenchmarks (see perf notes) Migration notes: existing clients using `function_call` will be unaffected unless they opt into new `compat.openai_tool_integration=false`. New behavior: inline injection will interleave tool text into the token stream; consumers using bytewise streaming should handle small injection markers. For programmatic integrations set `inject_results=metadata` to receive a stable structured envelope. Performance: benchmarked on an internal workload (mix of 70% cache-hit tools, small payloads) showing median request latency +12ms in ordered-parallel compare to baseline for 3-tool bursts; tail latency (p99) improved by ~8% when using ordered-parallel vs naive sequential orchestration due to early streaming of completed results. Files of interest: redwood/api/handler/tool_orchestrator.py, redwood/openai/compat/tool_mapper.py, redwood/runtime/scheduler/orchestrator.cpp, redwood/sdk-python/redwood/tools.py, redwood/sdk-typescript/src/tools.ts, docs/api/toolings.md, tests/integration/test_tool_orchestration.py, tests/e2e/test_streaming_injection.py. Risks & mitigations: - Streaming stability: Introduced streaming placeholders which we validated under e2e load tests; fallback policy to disable inline streaming injection if a node reports degraded streaming performance. - Backpressure: orchestrator respects request-level concurrency caps and signals head-of-line stalls back to the serving runtime. - Semantic shifts: default retry policy chosen conservatively; customers can override per-tool to avoid surprise duplicate executions. Related work: builds on internal perf improvements in ENG-2914 (scheduler batching) and references earlier tool-choreography PRs. Example request (pseudo): {"model":"rwd-1", "prompt":"Summarize and act", "tool_batch":[{"name":"search","input":"query","retry_policy":{"max_retries":2}},{"name":"db_read","input":"key","optional":true}], "tool_run_mode":"ordered-parallel","inject_results":"metadata"}

review_comments: Daniel Park (review): Overall design looks solid. A few requests: 1) Can we expose a global `max_parallel_tools` at request-time to avoid DoS-like bursts? 2) Need clearer failure mode example when an optional tool fails repeatedly. Also please add more unit tests around ordering edge cases.

Maya Chen (author): Added `max_parallel_tools` to the request schema with a sane server-side upper bound and documented failure modes in the migration notes. Added new unit tests covering partial completion + late-arriving results.

Ava Martinez (review): Concern about OpenAI compat mapping — can we keep the legacy function_call exact behavior when compat toggle is enabled (no change to inject_results)? Also please run compatibility smoke tests against a sample function-calling integration.

Maya Chen (author): Yes — compat.openai_tool_integration=true preserves exact legacy mapping (inline injection at the same offsets). Ran compatibility smoke suite against function-calling examples and added results to the PR description.
Ravi Singh (review): Minor: rename `inject_results=inline` marker to include an explicit sentinel token so streaming parsers can detect injection boundaries without heuristic parsing.
Maya Chen (author): Implemented sentinel token \uFFF9TOOL_INJECT\uFFFA and added parser helpers in SDKs. Documented in streaming notes.

notes: Hotfix follow-up planned: small perf tuning for orchestrator memory footprint (ENG-3350). Feature flag `tool_injection_v1` enabled in main and rollout via Console. SDKs bumped: python 1.8.0, typescript 1.6.0. Observability dashboard added under Console > Tools > Orchestration.
perf_notes: Bench harness (scripts/perf/tool_bench.py) used 8xA10G cluster, 10k synthetic requests with 3-tool layout: median added latency 12ms (ordered-parallel), p99 reduced by 8% compared to client-side sequential orchestration. Retry overhead measured: average increased token cost <0.5% under default retry policy.
